the System V ABI it turns out that there's this discussion of how the stack should look like when you're using a base pointer and so we have the things you might ex expect about arguments potentially up here above the return address uh sort of looking like the shadow stack so they're not necessarily going to be used that way we'll see more about that when we look at multiple function parameters later on return address and then rbp and so rbp minus something is typically going to be your local

variables and then there's this discussion of an area called the red zone so specifically it says the 128-byte area beyond the location pointed to by rsp is considered to be reserved and shall not be modified by signal or interrupt handlers therefore functions may use this area as temporary data that is not needed across function calls in particular leaf functions may use this area for their entire stack frame rather than adjusting the stack pointer in the prologue and epilogue this area

is known as the red zone so essentially what it's saying is normally you might see a function prolog subtract rsp down to here to allocate space for the local variables and then add rsp back up when you're leaving the function but it's saying if you're in a leaf function you can go ahead and just not bother with the subtract and the add go ahead and just use this area below where rbp and rsp would be both pointing right here go ahead and just use it because we know that your function is a leaf function

it's not going to call anything else and so it should just be you know used and then destroyed immediately when it goes out of scope so basically that's why it's allowed to get away with accessing below the bottom of the stack like this it'll be safe because they define in the ABI that you know exception handlers if some sort of interrupt occurs it shall not you know clobber over these things so you can resume from the interrupt without destroying your stack data which would you know ruin the program execution so
